title: Repository CI optimisation governance
purpose: Record design-only governance for CI timing visibility and parent CI optimisation closure without workflow changes, dashboard implementation, timing reports, proof execution, or readiness claims.

nonClaims: No CI workflow change is authorised by this artifact.
No CI timing dashboard is implemented by this artifact.
No timing report or measured performance claim is made by this artifact.
No proof, readiness, staging, production, deployment, compliance, store, release, live-provider, or human-acceptance claim is made.

observedCiState.interpretation: The current CI optimisation surface can be governed through explicit workflow, command, cache, timing, and report boundaries. Timing visibility is a future reporting concern and does not by itself alter required checks or proof expectations.

policyRules: A future CI timing dashboard or report must identify workflow, job, command, cache state, dependency state, environment, provider mode where relevant, and raw evidence source.
Timing reports are generated reports and must not be treated as semantic authority or proof readiness by themselves.
A timing dashboard may support regression triage, but it must not replace required validators, proof commands, evidence collection, or owner decisions.
Unknown timing provenance, missing raw evidence, stale report state, or environment mismatch must fail closed for performance claims.

preserved: CI timing visibility remains diagnostic rather than authoritative.
Required checks and proof gates remain separate from performance reporting.
Generated timing reports remain lower authority than raw execution evidence.
risk: Timing dashboards can create false confidence if cache state and raw evidence are missing.
Dashboard-only regressions can be overinterpreted as proof failures or readiness evidence requirements without explicit thresholds.
Mandatory timing collection can add CI cost if not scoped deliberately.

validationProofExpectation: Future implementation must preserve raw timing evidence before producing generated dashboard summaries.
Future CI budget enforcement requires a separate owner decision and explicit threshold policy.
Future dashboard publication must preserve the generated-report boundary and fail closed on stale or unknown timing status.
dependenciesRecorded: USF-384 baseline timing and cost measurement
USF-860 owner decision: enforce performance budgets in CI
USF-861 owner decision: require command timing reports on every PR
ciTimingDashboardPolicy.ownerDecisionStatus: Current repository optimisation realisation approves evaluation of CI timing dashboards, performance budgets, and per-PR timing reports as timing options. Enforcement is not imposed until thresholds, raw timing evidence, provenance, and no-regression behaviour are defined.

parentCiOptimisationClosurePolicy.closureBasis: The remaining open child under USF-359 was the CI timing dashboard design issue. Parent closure is valid only as governance closure and does not implement or require a dashboard, CI budget, workflow mutation, or timing report.
nonClosureBoundaries: CI workflow optimisation is in evaluation scope and requires implementation evidence before any workflow-change claim.
Timing dashboard implementation is in evaluation scope and requires raw timing evidence, provenance, and generated-report boundaries before any dashboard claim.
Actual performance budget enforcement is in scope for evaluation but is not enforced until thresholds and raw timing evidence are defined.
Actual per-PR timing report requirement is in scope for evaluation but is not mandatory until overhead, provenance, and no-regression behaviour are defined.
